payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the source mug's requested move to the right of the headphones complete, incomplete with visible progress, or not made?
node.criteria: Pass only if visual correspondence establishes that the source mug is positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image, satisfying the requested move. Fail if the source mug is identifiable and remains at its source-side position with no visible progress toward the right. Also fail if the source mug is identifiable and evidence establishes that it has not moved toward the right, even if unrelated objects or edits are present. If the source mug's appearance or location has visibly changed, or a plausible corresponding mug has moved toward the right while remnants remain, treat this as incomplete progress and fail rather than pass. Do not count a right-side mug alone as completion, or infer no progress solely from a pale mug left of the headphones or an indistinct blue patch at the source location. Use unknown only when source-to-edited correspondence or whether any progress occurred cannot be determined from the images.
node.binding: Compare the source image's light-blue mug—including its body shape, handle, appearance, scale, and original position left of the headphones—with all mug-like objects and visible remnants in the edited image. Assess the pale mug left of the headphones, the mug right of them, and the blue-looking blurred patch at far left as possible correspondence evidence. Altered color, size, or appearance alone does not rule out identity; neither the patch nor the left mug conclusively establishes identity or lack of movement. Determine whether the source mug is visibly to the right of the headphones, has plausibly moved toward the right but remains short of the requested position, or shows no discernible progress. Base the decision on source-to-edited visual evidence and the requested move, not mug count or right-side position alone; retain unknown if correspondence or progress remains genuinely indeterminate.

node_traces.evidence: The source light-blue mug is left of the headphones. In the edited image, a pale mug remains left of the headphones, while a separate mug is to their right; the source mug’s distinctive light-blue appearance is also visible as a blurred patch at far left. The source mug is not established as the right-side mug, and the visible evidence indicates no completed move to the right of the headphones.
